# S1 matrix (generated by `run_matrix.py`; do not edit by hand)

Cell values: `ok` = client succeeded and the repository passes `git fsck --strict --full` with the expected tip and object count; `REJECT` = client failed; `CORRUPT` = client reported success but the repository does not verify. `(dupN)` = N duplicate object ids written into the client's .idx files. `control-bad-count` is a negative control: `REJECT` is the correct result there.

## Scenarios

Counts describe the input segments; the last two columns describe the pack actually sent. `Hidden cycles` = deltas that only resolve through an external copy of an object the pack also contains (a delta cycle that `--fix-thin` hides).

| Scenario | Stitcher | Segments | Client has | Entries in | Duplicates in | Cross-segment REF_DELTA | Forward REF_DELTA | Thin REF_DELTA | Entries sent | Hidden cycles | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `control-single` | plain | FULL | - | 73 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 73 | 0 | Control: one ordinary full pack, no stitching. |
| `control-bad-count` | badcount | FULL | - | 73 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 73 | - | Negative control: header count off by one. Every client must reject it. |
| `clone-3seg` | plain | A+B+C | - | 73 | 0 | 21 | 0 | 0 | 73 | 0 | Clone from three stored packs A+B+C. B and C are thin, so their REF_DELTA bases are in earlier segments. |
| `thin-2seg` | plain | B+C | A | 28 | 0 | 3 | 0 | 18 | 28 | 0 | Incremental fetch: client has C3, gets B+C. Some REF_DELTA bases exist only in the client's repository (thin pack). |
| `reverse-order` | plain | C+B+A | - | 73 | 0 | 21 | 21 | 0 | 73 | 0 | Segments in reverse order C+B+A: REF_DELTA bases appear after the deltas that need them. |
| `overfetch-have` | plain | A+B+C | AB | 73 | 0 | 21 | 0 | 0 | 73 | 0 | Client has C5 but is sent A+B+C: every object of A and B is already in the client's repository. |
| `dup-overlap` | plain | AB+B+C | - | 91 | 18 | 21 | 0 | 0 | 91 | 0 | Overlapping cover: AB+B+C. Objects of B appear twice, encoded differently (full/OFS_DELTA in AB, REF_DELTA in B). |
| `dup-exact` | plain | A+A+B+C | - | 118 | 45 | 21 | 0 | 0 | 118 | 0 | The same segment twice: A+A+B+C. Every object of A appears twice with identical bytes. |
| `dup-thin` | plain | B+FULL | A | 91 | 18 | 14 | 14 | 0 | 91 | 0 | Client has C3, gets B+FULL. Objects of B appear twice, and B's thin bases are also in FULL. |
| `sc-single` | plain | Bsc | A | 30 | 0 | 0 | 14 | 0 | 30 | 0 | One stored self-contained push pack (Bsc) sent as-is, client has C3. No stitching; its completed bases sit after the deltas that use them. |
| `sc-clone` | plain | A+Bsc+Csc | - | 92 | 19 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 92 | 0 | Clone from self-contained push packs A+Bsc+Csc (as stored after S3). Completed bases duplicate objects of earlier packs. |
| `sc-fetch` | plain | Bsc+Csc | A | 47 | 3 | 0 | 18 | 0 | 47 | 0 | Client has C3, gets Bsc+Csc. Completed bases duplicate objects the client has and objects of Bsc. |
| `dup-thin+naive` | naive | B+FULL | A | 91 | 18 | 14 | 14 | 0 | 73 | 14 | dup-thin with naive dedupe (keep first copy, OFS->REF in touched segments). Creates 2-object delta cycles. |
| `reverse-order+topo` | topo | C+B+A | - | 73 | 0 | 21 | 21 | 0 | 73 | 0 | reverse-order with the topological stitcher (deltas moved after their bases). |
| `dup-overlap+topo` | topo | AB+B+C | - | 91 | 18 | 21 | 0 | 0 | 73 | 0 | dup-overlap with the topological stitcher (duplicates dropped). |
| `dup-exact+topo` | topo | A+A+B+C | - | 118 | 45 | 21 | 0 | 0 | 73 | 0 | dup-exact with the topological stitcher. |
| `dup-thin+topo` | topo | B+FULL | A | 91 | 18 | 14 | 14 | 0 | 73 | 0 | dup-thin with the topological stitcher: no cycles, still thin. |
| `sc-single+topo` | topo | Bsc | A | 30 | 0 | 0 | 14 | 0 | 30 | 0 | sc-single through the topological stitcher (bases moved first). |
| `sc-clone+topo` | topo | A+Bsc+Csc | - | 92 | 19 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 73 | 0 | sc-clone with the topological stitcher. |
| `sc-fetch+topo` | topo | Bsc+Csc | A | 47 | 3 | 0 | 18 | 0 | 44 | 0 | sc-fetch with the topological stitcher. |
| `thin-2seg+bases` | topo+bases | B+C | A | 28 | 0 | 3 | 0 | 18 | 44 | 0 | thin-2seg for a client without thin-pack: external bases sent whole in front. |
